claims.statement: EU law defines energy performance contracting around monitored and verified improvement and lists transparent measurement and verification of guaranteed savings among minimum contract items.
The revised buildings framework introduces renovation passports and policy pressure for staged renovations, creating more projects whose estimated and realised energy performance must be reconciled.
Hypothesis: an independent, lower-cost settlement layer can unlock performance guarantees for projects too small for traditional ESCO overhead, but installer and financier willingness must be tested.

contrary_evidence: Energy savings are sensitive to weather, occupancy, energy prices, and operational changes, so a simple before-and-after comparison is not dispute-grade.
Large ESCOs already have measurement practices; the unproven opening is an independent product for smaller contracts.

economics.acquisition_route: Family installer pilot, white-label inclusion in installer quotes, energy-auditor referrals, and lender risk teams
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1,500 monitored sites at a 300 PLN blended monthly fee yields 5.4m PLN ARR before setup and settlement fees; a profitable majority-owned monitoring platform could pass 5m PLN founder equity in four to seven years
economics.founder_time: Initially 15 hours weekly for method and integrations; target 8-10 hours weekly once field installation and audit review are delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: After remote ingestion is standardised, software monitoring can exceed 80% gross margin; field meters and auditor review reduce blended margin to an estimated 60-75%
economics.payback: One detected control fault or objectively resolved guarantee dispute can exceed several years of fees; target vendor CAC payback under nine months
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 2,000-6,000 PLN setup plus 180-600 PLN per building per month and a small fee on settled performance payments
economics.retention_or_repeat: Contracts naturally persist for 24-60 months and installers repeat across new sites if reports reduce disputes

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Normalised baseline-to-outcome data by building type, equipment, installer, weather, tariff, and operating pattern
fingerprint.customer: Installers, energy-service firms, lenders, property managers, and housing associations financing small-to-mid-sized retrofits
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded in installer and energy-auditor proposals, followed by lender and property-manager channel agreements
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Independent M&V setup, telemetry software, exception reports, and contract settlement as a recurring per-building service
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer, owner, or financier pays at baseline setup and monthly through the verification term, with optional settlement fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A retrofit proposal includes a savings promise, financing covenant, warranty dispute, or post-installation underperformance concern

founder_fit: Excellent quantitative and renewable-family fit: the founder can build baselines, anomaly detection, and automated reports while a qualified energy auditor validates methodology. A first family-company project can be bounded and part-time, with low personal-brand dependence.
risks: Disputes can create professional-liability exposure if the method is underspecified.
Hardware installation and data gaps can erode gross margin.
A financier or installer may prefer its own methodology and block a neutral layer.

structure.control_point: The mutually accepted baseline and authoritative calculation of realised savings
structure.critical_dependency: Installer, owner, and financier acceptance of the measurement method and data access

thesis: Provide independent baselining, telemetry normalisation, measurement, and settlement for heat-pump, insulation, solar, and control-system performance contracts. Start with small commercial buildings and housing associations where installers, lenders, or owners need a shared answer to whether promised savings occurred. The durable asset is a cross-vendor building-performance benchmark and a trusted settlement record.
title: Verified Retrofit Savings Rail
uncertainties: Minimum site size at which recurring telemetry and verification are economical.
Whether customers value neutral settlement enough to pay separately rather than rely on the installer.
Availability and consistency of meter, tariff, weather, and building-operation data in Poland.
